key_insight: The study introduces the Neurocognitive Speech Taxonomy (NST), an interpretable framework that maps voice features to 7 neurocognitive domains to support voice-based detection of Alzheimer’s-related cognitive impairment and biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: NST may help make AI voice biomarkers more interpretable and potentially more equitable than standard cognitive testing for identifying cognitive decline and AD-related changes.
method: Mapped 314 voice features to 7 neurocognitive domains
Validated structure, clinical validity, and equity across 3 cohorts (N=1,479)
Tested links to cognitive status, AD biomarker status, longitudinal change, and neuroimaging
evidence_signal: Across three cohorts, NST showed stable structure (Mantel r=0.71-0.77), distinguished MCI and AD biomarker status, and correlated with hippocampal volume (up to r=0.28).
watch_item: The framework needs broader external validation and real-world implementation testing before it can be relied on for clinical decision-making.
paper_title: A neurocognitive speech taxonomy for voice biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease
